To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide a general framework for the analysis of proximal Newton-type methods for convex optimization problems with locally Lipschitz gradients and inexact function evaluations.

we have proposed a new algorithm that can solve convex optimization problems, with self-concordant functions, data fidelity terms and regularizers, in a provable manner and that can be used for the recovery of sparse covariance matrices, which is of interest for many applications.

we prove attractive convergence rate results for the class of problems that include the sparse covariance estimation problem, we enhance state-of-the art optimization schemes to accommodate the presence of inexact gradient evaluations, and we provide experimental results on sparse covariance estimations that show the merits of the proposed method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of scalable algorithms for the estimation of sparse covariance matrices from high dimensional data.
the development of efficient and scalable optimization schemes for large-scale convex problems, which can be applied to many important applications.
the development of a novel optimization algorithm, which is suitable for a broad class of convex optimization problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is a powerful and flexible tool for solving a wide range of problems, with a number of attractive convergence properties.
the proposed method is able to provide state-of-the-art recovery performance, while at the same time being computationally more efficient.
the proposed algorithm is the best in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we have proposed a novel algorithm to estimate sparse covariance matrices and have shown that our algorithm is more efficient and robust to noise than the existing methods.
, we have developed a novel proximal Newton scheme for solving a large class of convex problems, and that we have shown that it can be applied to the problem of sparse covariance estimation.

, we have developed a novel proximal Newton method for convex minimization problems and we have shown that the proposed algorithm is able to handle inexact function evaluations and it can be used in the context of sparse covariance estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under the self-concordant setting, the presence of inexact gradients does not affect the overall convergence rate.
inexact proximal Newton iterations can be a powerful tool in the optimization toolbox of practitioners, especially in high dimensional settings.

, under a mild assumption on the data fidelity function, we are able to provide an algorithm that provably achieves a linear rate of convergence, with a computational cost of the order of the number of iterations.
